problem: The lead says the system must "meter, atomise, distribute and time the fuel", listing four jobs, but Section 1 correctly lists five (pressure is missing). A student reading only the lead gets an incomplete list that conflicts with the rest of the chapter.
fix: Change the last sentence of the lead to: "The system must meter, atomise, distribute, time and pressurise the fuel."

problem: Distributor (rotary) pump systems are named as direct-injection examples, but distributor pumps are used on both direct-injection and indirect-injection (prechamber) diesel engines. The figure also leaves distributor pump out, so text and figure disagree about the examples of direct injection.
fix: Write: "Common rail and unit injector systems are direct; distributor pump systems can be either, depending on whether the injector sprays into the cylinder or into a prechamber." Add distributor pump to the direct branch of the figure, or state that the figure shows only two representative examples.

problem: Grouping petrol port injection and throttle body injection under "indirect injection" goes beyond standard usage, where indirect injection means a diesel prechamber or swirl chamber. The reasoning (fuel meets air outside the cylinder) is sound, but the label will confuse a student who meets the standard textbook definition.
fix: Add one sentence: "Strictly, textbooks use indirect injection for the diesel prechamber; for petrol engines the same idea is called port or manifold injection, because the fuel meets the air outside the cylinder."

problem: "Continuous injection sprays all the time; intermittent injection sprays in pulses" gives no example of either, so the distinction stays abstract.
fix: Add: "Intermittent injection is used by almost every modern diesel and petrol engine; continuous injection appears only in a few special petrol systems and in some gas engines."

problem: The references "See 2.3", "see 2.4" and "see chapter 2.9" are plain text, so a student reading on a phone cannot jump to them.
fix: Mark them as chapter links, for example chapter 2.3 and chapter 2.4, using the same ids as the other chapters.

problem: "Solid injection is the working family" is unclear; "working" could be read as "functioning" or as "the family that does the work".
fix: Write: "Notice that solid (airless) injection is the family used on modern engines, and that common rail and unit injector are examples of the direct branch."
